key_insight: Sub-yield aging and over-yield rejuvenation in metallic glass are governed by one dynamic scaling framework, but with different energy-injection pathways: macroscopic plastic work above yield and localized elastic stress fluctuations below yield.
engineering_relevance: This provides a predictive basis for tuning cyclic loading conditions to either stabilize amorphous structures through aging or deliberately rejuvenate them for property control in metallic glass components.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of a cyclically driven metallic glass
Compare sub-yield and over-yield regimes through nonlinear rheology and stress fluctuation analysis
Derive a scaling identity linking relaxation attenuation to stress fluctuation exponents
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a unified dynamic clock and exact scaling relation supported by simulation results that connect Herschel-Bulkley rheology with localized stress fluctuation dynamics.
watch_item: The framework is simulation-based, so experimental validation across compositions, temperatures, and loading histories will be needed before broad design use.
paper_title: Universal Dynamic Scaling for Sub-Yield Aging and Over-Yield Rejuvenation in A Cyclically Driven Metallic Glass
